supersedes.reason: The v1 post-hoc protocol covered only within-turn-correction; the primary paper unambiguously defines four raw tags as the user-revision family. The v1 file remains immutable historical evidence.

paper.title: PRESTO: A Multilingual Dataset for Parsing Realistic Task-Oriented Dialogs
paper.finding: The authors explicitly group correct-action, correct-argument, within-turn-correction, and cancel-action under the broader user-revision linguistic phenomenon.

pinned_repository.finding: The pinned README identifies revisions as a target phenomenon, documents the raw linguistic_phenomena field, and points to the primary paper for the taxonomy.

observed_before_protocol.original_failure: revision bucket absent, so required hard-bucket representation and gap checks failed

claim_limits: The original preregistered result remains a failed gate and is never rewritten.
The corrected gate is a post-hoc diagnostic, not a preregistered keep decision.
The completed training view replayed zero revision examples because the same v1 taxonomy was used during focus selection; post-hoc rescoring cannot repair that intervention.
The aggregate revision result must be accompanied by all four raw-tag metrics so strong subgroups cannot hide a weak subgroup.
No official PRESTO test, native PRESTO metric, Mobile Actions regression, hidden safety suite, seed replication, or larger-model comparison is evaluated.
